comments.body:
## Prior art, and why this is a follow-on rather than a duplicate

Two closed tickets cover adjacent ground. Neither closes this gap.

**`fd6b-09c5-8f76-45ad`** ("docs/exit-codes.md has drifted from ROUTES and advertises a
gate it lacks", mirror F12) is the ticket that ADDED the parity test. Before it, the only
assertion touching the file was `assert "\`11\`" in text and "block-but-retryable" in
text.lower()` -- nothing checked the table at all. fd6b fixed that and narrowed the
file's claim on the **exit-value** axis (`:12-15`: "those columns are hand-authored").
It did not qualify the claim on the **nesting** axis, which is what this bug reports.

**`f0ff-028a-f5cb-4b66`** ("Make docs/exit-codes.md complete and keep it that way") is the
sharper one. It closed with this acceptance criterion ticked:

> - [x] A CI check asserts every dispatcher arm has a row, so a new command without one
>       fails

That criterion is **not satisfied as written**, and this ticket is the demonstration.
`rebar store build-vectors` is a new dispatcher arm. It shipped with no row. `make verify`
passed twice. The omission was caught by an LLM code-review advisory on Gerrit change
3218, not by CI.

The criterion is satisfied only under a reading of "dispatcher arm" that means top-level
route, which is not how the surrounding description uses it -- f0ff's own description
counts "75 real commands ... from `_cli/_help.known_subcommands()` union
`_cli/__init__._INTERCEPTS`", a set that necessarily includes nested members, against
`_live_route_names()`'s 53.

So the enforcement gap is not a regression since f0ff; it is the gap f0ff believed it had
closed. That makes the documentation route (narrow the claim) and the enforcement route
(make the claim true) a genuine choice rather than a formality, and it is why this ticket
offers both and requires the chosen one to be demonstrated by mutation rather than
asserted. f0ff's AC was ticked without such a demonstration, which is how it came to be
wrong.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Implemented at 879fc8bae93 (worktree impl-e095, branch impl-e095, based on origin/main af769ead9fe).

## What the gap actually was

`_live_route_names()` read only `ROUTES` (53 top-level). `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` exports a **second** tuple alongside it — `STORE_ROUTES` (`:532`, builder `_store_routes()` at `:444`), 8 members on origin/main. The parity test's `orphaned` check keyed each doc row on `row.split()[0]`, so all 9 `store <member>` rows matched the live `store` route no matter which member they named. Both directions were unenforced for those rows: a row for a deleted member passed, and a live member with no row passed.

Note for anyone reading the ticket's Evidence section: `_live_route_names` is at `:246`, not `:247`.

## Change

- `_NESTED_REGISTRIES = ("store",)` — only `store` has a member registry. Measured: of 82 table rows, 19 are nested, by parent `store 10, bridge 3, check 2, deps 1, list 1, resolve 1, show 1`. The other 6 parents dispatch through their own parsers, so 10 rows are structurally uncoverable and the doc now says so instead of implying full coverage.
- `_live_route_names()` unions `f"store {route.name}"` for non-retired `STORE_ROUTES`.
- `orphaned` now keys a row on its two-token prefix when its first token is in `_NESTED_REGISTRIES`, else the first token.

Exact row-to-route equality was not viable: `store compact --all` is a flag variant with no route of its own. The two-token rule admits it because `store compact` is live.

Kept the row-key logic as an inline dict comprehension rather than a module-level helper, so it cannot register a `test_helper` mechanism. Confirmed: `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0.

## AC2 — enforcement demonstrated in both directions, with a control

Mutation 1 (live route loses its row): deleted the `store compact` row, giving
`AssertionError: ... live routes with no doc row: ['store compact']`. Restored byte-exact.

Mutation 2 (row names a member that does not exist): inserted a `store no-such-member` row, giving
`AssertionError: ... doc rows that do not name a live route: ['store no-such-member']`. Restored byte-exact.

Control, which is the part that proves the change is load-bearing rather than merely that tests fail: both mutations were replayed against the **origin/main** version of the test file. Both **passed**. The old test passes the mutants; the new test fails them.

## Gates run locally

- `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py` — 29 passed
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` — clean
- `ruff check --select C901` — clean
- `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` — exit 0
- `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` — exit 0

`make verify` is queued behind two other runs on this host (load average 57 from unrelated processes); push follows it.

## Ordering dependency on 0461

e095's enforcement is currently satisfied on origin/main: 8 store routes, 8 rows. 0461 (Gerrit 3218) adds the `build-vectors` **route** without its table **row**, so landing 3218 unamended would make main red the moment e095 lands. 3218 has now been amended to carry the row (commit 3401b613dd2, Change-Id preserved), which removes the hazard.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Verify triage: the 18 failures recorded earlier were an environment error, not repository evidence.

What happened: `make verify` in `.rebar/worktrees/impl-e095` ran under
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.rebar/worktrees/impl-0461/.venv/bin/python` — a
*different* worktree's interpreter. That venv's editable install resolves
`rebar.__file__` to impl-0461's `src/rebar/__init__.py`. The whole-tree AST
helpers compute `_REPO_ROOT` from `tests/_tree_scan.py`'s own location
(`tests/_tree_scan.py:13`) but reach `src/rebar` through the imported package,
so `ParsedModule.__init__` called
`PosixPath('.../impl-0461/src/rebar/__init__.py').relative_to('.../impl-e095')`
and raised `ValueError`. Every failure was one of those scans — "appears only
in", "exactly one definition under src", the engine-dir resolution tests.

Measured: impl-e095 has its own `.venv`, and
`.venv/bin/python -c "import rebar; print(rebar.__file__)"` returns
`.../impl-e095/src/rebar/__init__.py`. Re-running all 12 affected modules under
that interpreter: **138 passed in 78s, 0 failures.**

This is the failure mode AGENTS.md's Codex environment rule names — a toolchain
resolved from outside the worktree is an environment error, and the rule applies
to pytest for the same reason it applies to ruff and mypy. The earlier report
of "18 failures" overstated what had been established; it was never checked
which interpreter produced them.

State of the change: one commit, `92ec49b1143`, clean tree, Change-Id
`Ic0d44614099e9bedce25978fa723253aa70f4819`, not yet pushed to Gerrit (queried;
no matching change exists). Remaining before push: a full `make verify` run
under this worktree's own `.venv`, deferred only to avoid CPU contention with
fe94's verify currently running on the same host.

Unverified: whether the full suite is green beyond these 12 modules. Only the
previously-failing set has been re-measured.

comments.body:
AC evidence, measured at the merged commit `664df6568f7` on `origin/main`.

Both routes were taken, so AC2 and AC3 both apply.

**AC1 — the doc no longer claims a guarantee the test does not make.** The
coverage sentence now reads that the cross-check "covers top-level routes and
the members of `store` (the one nested group with its own route registry)" and
names `bridge`, `check`, `deps`, `list`, `resolve`, `show` as convention rather
than gate.

**AC2 — enforcement demonstrated by mutation, both directions.** Baseline:
`test_exit_codes.py -k 'table or parity or route'` = 2 passed.
- Removed the live `| \`store fsck\` |` row ->
  `test_every_live_route_is_documented_and_every_doc_row_names_a_real_route`
  FAILED: "live routes with no doc row: ['store fsck']".
- Inverse: inserted an invented `| \`store nonexistent-member\` |` row -> same
  test FAILED: "doc rows that do not name a live route: ['store
  nonexistent-member']".
Doc restored; `git status` clean; full module = 29 passed.

**AC3 — the narrowed wording measured against `_live_route_names()`, not
asserted.** Loaded the test module and called it directly: 62 live routes = 53
top-level + 9 nested. All 9 nested entries are `store` members (`build-vectors`,
`compact`, `doctor`, `export`, `footprint`, `fsck`, `fsck-recover`, `import`,
`maintenance`). `store` is the ONLY nested parent in the live set, and none of
the 6 convention parents appears nested. That is exactly what the doc claims.

**AC4 — `make verify` passes.** Evidenced by `Verified +1` from the rebar CI bot
on Gerrit 3253 at revision `92ec49b1143`, GitHub Actions run 41587734110
(conclusion: success). That run's gating cell selects the same tier `make test`
selects.

Change 3253 merged 2026-11-02 22:48 PST as `664df6568f7`.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`docs/exit-codes.md` declares itself (`:5-6`) "the single source of truth for ... which
code each subcommand emits", and states (`:8-12`) that
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py` "cross-checks this file's per-command
table against the route registry, so a route with no row here ... fails the build."

That guarantee holds only for **top-level** routes. It does not hold for nested
subcommands, which is where most of the table's rows live.

## Evidence

`_live_route_names()` (`test_exit_codes.py:246-249`) builds
`{route.name for route in ROUTES if not route.retired}`. Measured on the live registry:

    'store' in live          -> True
    'build-vectors' in live  -> False
    'footprint' in live      -> False
    len(live)                -> 53

The parity test's own docstring is accurate and says so plainly: "each table
row begins with a live top-level route. Nested invocations share that route." The
`orphaned` check keys on `row.split()[0]` (`:264`), so a row for any `store <member>` is
accepted because `store` is live, and the `undocumented` check (`:259-263`) can never
demand a row for a member because no member name is in `live`.

Net effect: a new nested subcommand can land with no row, and nothing fails. Observed
directly -- `rebar store build-vectors` (ticket 0461-09ce-4850-42a7) passed `make verify`
twice with no row in the table. The gap was caught by an LLM code-review advisory, not
by the build.

The table nonetheless carries a row for every other `store` member, so the convention is
real and maintained by hand while the doc describes it as enforced.

## Why this matters beyond one missing row

This is the same defect class the file already documents about itself at `:12-15`:
"Until 2026-09 this file claimed a stronger guarantee than any test made, and the table
had drifted in both directions while carrying that claim." That correction narrowed the
claim on the *exit-value* axis (those columns are hand-authored) but left the
*row-coverage* claim unqualified, and on the nesting axis it is still too strong.

A doc that overstates its own enforcement is worse than one that states none: a reader
who trusts the claim has no reason to check the table by hand, which is exactly how the
`build-vectors` row came to be missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `docs/exit-codes.md` no longer claims a guarantee the parity test does not make:
      the row-coverage sentence states that enforcement covers top-level routes and
      that nested-subcommand rows are maintained by convention -- OR the parity test is
      extended so the claim becomes true.
- [x] If the enforcement route is taken, a test fails when a live nested subcommand has
      no row, demonstrated by a mutation (remove one existing member row; the test
      must fail) and by the inverse (an invented member row names a real nested
      invocation or the test fails).
- [x] If the documentation route is taken, the narrowed wording is shown to be accurate
      against `_live_route_names()` as measured, not asserted.
- [x] `make verify` passes.

## Out of scope

The missing `store build-vectors` row itself -- that is fixed in 0461-09ce-4850-42a7's
own change, which is where the omission arose.

## Implementation plan

Cites re-measured against this worktree on 2026-11-01; `_live_route_names` is at `:246`,
not `:247` as the Evidence section above originally said.

### A second route registry the Evidence section missed

"No member name is in `live`" is correct for `ROUTES`. But `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py`
builds and exports a **second** tuple beside it:

    ROUTES: tuple[Route, ...] = _build_routes()        # :441
    STORE_ROUTES: tuple[Route, ...] = _store_routes()  # :532 (builder at :444)

Both are in `__all__` (`:24-35`). Measured:

    len(ROUTES) -> 53 ; len(STORE_ROUTES) -> 9
    sorted(r.name for r in STORE_ROUTES) -> build-vectors, compact, doctor, export,
      footprint, fsck, fsck-recover, import, maintenance

`route.group` is a capability bucket (`reads_init_only`, `lookups`, ...), **not** a parent
command, so qualifying `ROUTES` by group yields nothing; `STORE_ROUTES` is the only
machine-readable registry of nested members. Enforcement for `store` is therefore cheap.

### Scope limit, measured

Of 82 table rows, 19 are nested, by parent:

    store 10, bridge 3, check 2, deps 1, list 1, resolve 1, show 1

Only `store` has a registry; the other 6 parents dispatch through their own parsers with
nothing to check against. Enforcement covers 9 nested rows and cannot cover the other 10.

This plan therefore takes **both** routes the ACs offer as alternatives: enforce where a
registry exists, narrow the wording where none does. Taking only the enforcement route
would leave the doc's claim still false for the 10 unenforceable rows.

### Changes

1. `_live_route_names()` (`:246-249`): union in `f"store {r.name}" for r in STORE_ROUTES
   if not r.retired`, keeping the existing `not retired` filter. Returns 62 names.

2. `orphaned` (`:264`) currently keys on `row.split()[0]`, which would let an invented
   `store no-such-member` row pass and so would not satisfy AC2's inverse. Replace with:
   for a row whose first token is a parent that has a registry, require the two-token
   prefix to be live; otherwise keep first-token matching. Measured consequence: the one
   row with no matching route, `store compact --all`, still passes because its two-token
   prefix `store compact` is live.

3. Update the parity test's docstring, which reads "each table row begins with a live
   top-level route" -- accurate today, wrong after change 1.

4. `docs/exit-codes.md:10-12`: state what is actually enforced (top-level routes plus
   `store` members) and that rows under the other nested parents are convention.

### Demonstration (AC2)

- Mutation: delete the `store compact` row; `undocumented` must report `store compact`
  and the test must fail. Restore, confirm byte-exact.
- Inverse: add a row `store no-such-member`; after change 2 `orphaned` must report it and
  the test must fail. Both mutants are run and shown failing, not argued.

### Ordering

`store build-vectors` has no row on `origin/main`; 0461-09ce-4850-42a7 adds it. Change 1
makes a missing member row a failure, so this change must land **after** 0461 or it
breaks the build. Not a blocker on starting work -- only on pushing.

### Files

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`, `docs/exit-codes.md`.

file_impact.reason: extend _live_route_names with STORE_ROUTES; tighten the orphaned check to a two-token rule for parents that have a registry; update the parity test docstring
narrow the row-coverage claim to what is enforced (top-level routes plus store members) and state that other nested rows are convention

compiled_state.title: exit-codes.md claims a route-row guarantee the parity test does not make for nested subcommands
